kept.excerpt: Argentina goals: Messi (29), L. Martinez (92), Borges (OG,111). The defending champions survived a pulsating match against a heroic Cabo Verde. Argentina will face Egypt in the last 16.
kept.relevance: FIFA credits Messi with one goal in Argentina’s round-of-32 victory and identifies the decisive goal as an own goal, which does not count toward Messi’s total.

kept.excerpt: Messi's goal in the 29th minute was the 20th of his World Cup career, extending his record and moving him two ahead of France's Kylian Mbappé on the all-time list. Messi was pictured later at his media conference with a large bump on his head after apparently being hit with a knee during a collision with a Cape Verde player. "It hurts a little but I'm good," he was quoted in comments translated from Spanish about the goose-egg over his right eye.
kept.relevance: The report corroborates Messi’s latest goal and provides contemporaneous information about a head collision and his stated condition.

kept.excerpt: Who: Argentina vs Egypt. What: FIFA World Cup 2026 – Round of 16. When: Tuesday, July 7, at 12pm (16:00 GMT). The winner of the Argentina vs Egypt match will play either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarterfinals in Kansas City in the US on Saturday, July 11.
kept.relevance: The cutoff-day preview establishes Argentina’s next fixture and conditional quarterfinal path, which determine Messi’s opportunities to add goals.

kept.excerpt: Lionel Messi came off the bench to score his sixth goal of the FIFA World Cup 2026™ as Argentina beat Jordan 3-1 in Dallas. He lashed home an 80th-minute free-kick to net for the seventh successive World Cup game, setting a new record. With top spot already confirmed ahead of the match, Messi was named among the substitutes as Lionel Scaloni made nine changes from the team that started their 2-0 win over Austria on Monday.
kept.relevance: FIFA establishes Messi’s six-goal group-stage tally and documents his substitute role in the final group match.

kept.excerpt: Argentina goals: Messi (17, 60, 76). Lionel Messi equalled the all-time FIFA World Cup™ goalscoring record with a hat-trick as Argentina kicked off their title defence with victory over Algeria in Group J at Kansas City Stadium.
kept.relevance: The official opening-match report documents the three goals that supplied half of Messi’s group-stage tally.

kept.excerpt: Messi scored seven times in the tournament, and twice in the final. His tally is only bettered by Kylian Mbappe, who became just the second player to score a hat-trick in a World Cup final, after Geoff Hurst in 1966.
kept.relevance: Messi’s seven-goal championship campaign in 2022 supplies an official historical benchmark for the ten-goal threshold.

kept.excerpt: France striker Just Fontaine astonishingly hit 13 goals in six games at Sweden 1958 – a record for one World Cup. He is followed by Hungary’s Sandor Kocsis (11 goals in 1954), West Germany’s Gerd Muller (10 in 1970), Brazil’s Ademir de Menezes (9 in 1950) and Portugal’s Eusebio (9 in 1966).
kept.relevance: FIFA’s pre-tournament historical ranking establishes how exceptional a double-digit individual World Cup goal tally has been.

search_notes: Frozen evidence cutoff: 2026-07-06, inclusive. All included items have explicit publication dates visible in web_search results on or before the cutoff; later-dated material, undated pages, rolling tournament summaries containing later developments, and betting or prediction-market pages were excluded. The included FIFA reports establish six goals after the group stage and one additional goal against Cabo Verde, implying seven goals through the round of 32 and three more needed to reach ten. Excerpts were taken from source text surfaced by web_search. Direct web_fetch failed because its provider was not configured; the requested agent-reach web-read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so full-page retrieval was unavailable and no further fallback attempts were made. These are dated-source extracts, not independently archived copies of the pages as they appeared at the cutoff.
